The fourth: it is the Torah, said by Ibn Bahr.

﴿On parchment spread out﴾. Regarding it there are three views:

The first: it is the unrolled page, which is what brings out people's deeds to them. Every page is called raqq because of the thinness of its margins. Al-Mutallammis said:

*As if it, from the age of its era, is a parchment whose book has been made available, inscribed.*

The second: it is paper written upon, said by Abu Ubaydah.

The third: it is what lies between the East and the West, said by Ibn Abbas.

[p. 378]

﴿And the Frequented House﴾. Regarding it there are four views:

The first: what Qatadah narrated from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was taken up to the heaven, and the Frequented House was raised up for us. Behold, it was directly opposite the Ka'bah. If it were to fall, it would fall upon it. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and when they leave it, they do not return to it." This was said by Ali and Ibn Abbas.

The second: what al-Suddi said: that the Frequented House is a house above the six heavens and below the seventh, called al-Durah. Seventy thousand angels from the tribe of Iblis pray in it every day, and they never return to it. It is directly opposite the Ancient House.

The third: what al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: that the Frequented House was on earth, at the site of the Ka'bah, in the time of Adam. When the time of Nuh came, he commanded them to perform Hajj, but they refused him and disobeyed him. When the water rose high, it was lifted and placed opposite it in the lowest heaven, where it is frequented. Then Allah settled Ibrahim at the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, where it had been. Allah, Most High, said: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾, and so on.

The fourth: what al-Hasan said: that the Frequented House is the Sacred House.

Regarding ﴿frequented﴾ (al-ma'mur) there are two views:

The first: that it is frequented by being intended.

The second: that it is frequented by staying at it. A poet said:

*The House was frequented by a frequenter, when the gazelles of the wild cows came to it, and gazelles of the morning came to it.*

Sahl interpreted it as the heart, whose frequenting is its sincerity, but this is far-fetched.

﴿And the Raised Ceiling﴾. Regarding it there are two views:

The first: it is the heaven, said by Ali.

The second: it is the Throne, said by al-Rabi'.

﴿And the Sea that is filled﴾ (al-bahr al-masjur). Regarding it there are three sayings:

The first: it is Jahannam (Hell), narrated by Safwan ibn Ya'la from the Prophet (ﷺ).

The second: it is a sea beneath the Throne, narrated by Abu Salih from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him).

The third: it is the sea of the earth, and this is the apparent meaning.

[p. 379]

Regarding His saying ﴿masjur﴾ there are seven interpretations:

The first: confined, said by Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi.

The second: released (al-mursal), said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: set aflame with fire, said by Mujahid.

The fourth: full, said by Qatadah.

The fifth: mixed, said by Ibn Bahr.

The sixth: one whose water has gone and dried up, narrated by Ibn Abi Wahshiyyah from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The seventh: one from whose water no one drinks and with which no crop is watered, said by al-Ala' ibn Zayd.

This is the end of the oath, and its answer is: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾. Al-Kalbi narrated that Jubayr ibn Mut'im came to Madinah to ransom a relative of his called Malik, who had been captured on the day of Badr. He found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying the [Maghrib] prayer and reciting ﴿By the Mount﴾, so he sat listening, until he reached His saying, Most High: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾. Jubayr then embraced Islam out of fear of the punishment, and began saying: "I did not think that I would rise from my place before the punishment befell me."

﴿On the day the heaven will shake violently﴾. Regarding it there are seven interpretations:

The first: its meaning is that it will turn around in a circle (taduru dawran), said by Mujahid. Tarafah ibn al-Abd said:

*Tawny-bearded, her neck-tendons firm, her hand moves flexibly, far-striding in her step.*

The second: it will surge in waves (tamuju mawjan), said by al-Dahhak.

The third: the heaven will split apart, said by Ibn Abbas, based on His saying, Most High: ﴿And when the mountains are crumbled to dust﴾, and so on.

The fourth: the heaven will flow in a flowing motion. From this is the saying of Jarir:

*The slain did not cease to flow their blood in the Tigris, until the water of the Tigris became mixed in color.*

The fifth: it will tilt over with its people, said by Abu Ubaydah, who recited the verse of al-A'sha:

[p. 380]

*As if her gait, from the house of her neighbor, is the swaying of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.*

The first: they will be pushed with a violent push. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet:

This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

The second: they will be driven with force, said by Qatadah.

Second: ﴿nāʿimīn﴾ (in ease and comfort), as said by Qatādah.

Third: ﴿fariḥīn﴾ (rejoicing), as said by al-Suddī.

Second: they are joined with gold (al-mawṣūlah bil-dhahab).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 52, verse 21–28:

﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in belief﴾. Regarding this, there are four interpretations:

The first: Allah admits the descendants into Paradise by virtue of their fathers' faith. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: Allah grants the descendants the like of their fathers' rewards without the fathers' rewards being diminished in any way. This was said by Ibrahim (al-Nakhaʿi).

The third: They are the adults who did acts of obedience to Allah along with their fathers, so Allah joins them to their fathers. This was said by Qatadah.

The fourth: When their children reach the deeds that their fathers performed, they follow them in those deeds and become like them in them. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

(p-382) ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. Regarding this, there are two interpretations:

One of them: "We did not diminish them," as said by Ibn ʿAbbas. Ru'bah said:

"A night of travel I traveled, and no lion-like one of its journey turned me back"

That is, it did not diminish me. The meaning of the statement is: the fathers are not diminished by what We gave the children.

The second: its meaning is "and We did not wrong them." This was said by Ibn Jubayr. Al-Hutay'ah said:

"Convey to the chiefs of Banu Saʿd a message, the utmost effort of delivery, neither distorted (alta) nor false"

That is, neither wronging nor lying.

The meaning of the statement is: We did not wrong the fathers by what We gave the children; rather Allah did that for the children out of honour for the fathers.

﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾. Regarding this, there are two aspects:

One of them: accountability, just as rights are taken from pledges (rihan).

The second: that he is detained, and from it comes al-rahn (the pledge), because of its being held back by the right. The poet said:

"I never feared that I would become a pledge to a red-faced Coptic-born freed man of the people"

﴿They pass to one another a cup﴾. That is, they hand it to each other and pass it around, one giving to another, namely the believer, his wives and his servants in Paradise.

The kas (cup) is a vessel filled with drink or other things; it is called a kas, but when it is emptied it is no longer called a kas. The evidence for tanazuʿ (passing) and kas in the language is the saying of al-Akhtal:

"A drinker, pleasantly intoxicated with the cup, made me his companion, neither by presence nor in it with a sawar... The sweet wine of the noble vintage contended with him, when the rooster crowed and the time of the night-traveler's arrival came."

﴿No idle talk therein, nor any sinfulness﴾. Regarding this, there are four aspects:

One of them: there is no falsehood in the wine and no sin, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah; that is only in this world, from Satan.

The second: there is no lying in it nor breaking of promises, as said by al-Dahhak.

The third: they do not revile one another over it, nor does one of them charge another with sin, as said by Mujahid.

(p-383) The fourth: there is no idle talk in Paradise nor lying; this is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Here, laghw means foul speech, as Dhu al-Rummah said:

"Neither foulness nor obscenity is among them, nor is there awe in them other than what it is... A man of firm, strong manliness, who does not desire the idle, babbling talk."

﴿And there will go around them youths belonging to them﴾. Ibn Bahr mentioned two aspects regarding this:

One of them: that the children are from their offspring who preceded them, and Allah thereby gladdens their eyes.

The second: that they are those whom Allah granted them as servants from the children of others.

﴿As if they were preserved pearls﴾. That is, protected by a covering and a veil, and from it is the poet's saying:

"I used to give them wealth and withhold my honour from them, and their affection is hidden in the breast."

Qatadah said: It has reached me that it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, these servants are like hidden pearls, so what of those they serve?" He said: (ﷺ) "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the superiority between them is like the superiority of the full moon night over the stars."

﴿So Allah has been gracious to us﴾. This may bear two meanings:

One of them: with Paradise and bliss.

The second: with success and guidance.

﴿And protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾. Regarding this, there are three aspects:

One of them: that it is the punishment of the Fire, as said by Ibn Zayd.

Al-Asamm said: al-Samum is one of the names of Hell.

The second: that it is the blaze of Hell, which is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Jurayj.

The third: the scorching of the sun and heat, and it may also be used for the scorching of cold, as the rajiz said:

"Today is a cold day, its samum is cold; because of the day's anguish, we do not blame it."

﴿Indeed, He is the Most Good, the Most Merciful﴾. Regarding this, there are three interpretations:

One of them: that al-Barr is the truthful, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

The second: the Gentle, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

(p-384) The third: that He is the doer of the well-known goodness (birr), as said by Ibn Bahr.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 52, verses 36–43:**

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?﴾ On this there are two views:

First: the keys of mercy.

Second: the treasuries of provision.

﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ On this there are four views:

First: they are those who have power over others (al-musallatun). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak.

Second: they are the lords (al-arbab). This was said by al-Hasan and Abu ʿUbayd.

Third: its meaning is: "Or are they the ones who manage affairs (al-mutawallun)?" This has also been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Fourth: they are the guardians (al-hafaza), derived from the writing of a book (tasTir al-kitab), which preserves what is written in it. So the musaytir (controller) here is one who preserves what Allah has written in the al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet). This was said by Ibn Bahr.

﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ On this there are two views:

First: the ladder is that which ascends to the heaven. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil:

*Neither the remoteness of lands protects a man,*
*nor are ladders built for him into the heavens.*

Second: it is the means by which one reaches lofty things. The poet said:

*You have wronged me with a fault, though I did not commit it,*
*so that you might take an excuse as a ladder to abandonment.*

His words ﴿by which they listen﴾ may bear two meanings:

First: they listen from the heaven to what Allah decrees for His creation.

Second: they listen from it to what Allah sends down to His messengers of revelation.

﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority.﴾ On this there are two views:

First: let their listener, i.e. their companion, bring a manifest proof that indicates the truth of his claim.

Second: let him bring a power that dominates the ears and indicates His power.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 52, verse 44–49:

﴿And if they should see a fragment (kisf) of the sky falling down﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

First: it means pieces of the sky; this is the view of Qatadah.

Second: a side of the sky.

Third: a punishment from the sky; this is the view of al-Mufaddal.

It is called kisf because it covers (taghtiyah), and al-kisf means covering; from it is derived the eclipse (kusuf) of the sun and the moon.

﴿They would say, "Layered cloud."﴾ Concerning "markum" (layered, piled up) there are two opinions:

First: it means thick, this is the view of Ibn Bahr.

Second: it means much, piled upon one another; this is the view of al-Dahhak.

The meaning of the verse is: if they were to see a fragment of the sky falling upon them as a punishment, they would not believe, and they would say, "It is a layered cloud, one part upon another."

﴿So leave them until they meet their Day﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

First: the day they die; this is the view of Qatadah.

Second: the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ula); related by Ibn Isa.

Third: the Day of Resurrection, when they will be struck senseless (yughsha 'alayhim) by the terror of what they witness. From it is the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious (sa'iqan)﴾, meaning, fainted.

﴿And indeed for those who have wronged there is a punishment short of that﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

First: the punishment of the grave; this is the view of Ali.

Second: hunger; this is the view of Mujahid.

Third: their affliction in this world; this is the view of al-Hasan.

Concerning who is meant by "those who have wronged" here there are two opinions:

First: they are the people of minor sins among the Muslims.

Second: they are among them those who commit the prescribed offences (hudud).

(p-387) ﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾. Concerning this there are two meanings:

First: for His decree concerning what He has entrusted you with of His message.

Second: for His trial concerning what He has tested you with from your people.

﴿Indeed, you are under Our eyes﴾. Concerning this there are three meanings:

First: under Our knowledge; this is the view of al-Suddi.

Second: in Our sight; related by Ibn Isa.

Third: under Our protection and safeguarding; from it is the saying of Allah to Musa, ﴿and that you may be raised under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39], meaning under My protection and safeguarding; this is the view of al-Dahhak.

﴿And glorify your Lord with praise when you arise﴾. Concerning this there are four sayings:

First: that he glorifies Allah when he rises from his gathering; this is the view of Abu al-Ahwas, so that it serves as expiation for what occurred in his day.

Second: when you rise from your sleep, so that the beginning of his work is with the remembrance of Allah; this is the view of Hassan ibn Atiyyah.

Third: when you rise from the midday nap for the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr); this is the view of Zayd ibn Aslam.

Fourth: it is the glorification in prayer when he stands to it.

Concerning this glorification there are two sayings:

First: it is the saying "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim" in bowing and "Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la" in prostration.

Second: the opening of prayer with the words "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika [wa tabaraka ismuka wa ta'ala jadduka wa la ilaha ghayruka]"; this is the view of al-Dahhak.

﴿And during the night glorify Him, and at the retreat of the stars﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

First: that it is the night prayer (salat al-layl).
